lessons.title: Places Around Town
lessons.goal: Name useful places, locate familiar people, and connect a place with a familiar need.
lessons.known: Units 1–3: people, books, colors, possessions, It is…, is/are. Unit 4: Where is…?, next to, first/then/after that/finally. Unit 5: I need…, food and polite requests.
lessons.story: Ana and her family make a short neighborhood visit. Start at the station, locate the father at the bank and the mother at the pharmacy, find the children at the library, then meet at the mall and get food at the supermarket. Explicit Spanish transitions explain each change of location; the English stays within the early lesson’s scope.
lessons.bridge: Now that we know the destinations, 6.2 introduces ways to travel to them.
lessons.evidence: Bank is already in the current Unit 6.1. It was not found as a declared target in Units 1–5. Keep it in this rebuild; do not call it a newly added course word. Mall and supermarket are proposed additions. Do not assess a hidden errand from a generic building photo.
lessons.reuse: 6.3 destination exchanges; 6.6 neighborhood search; 6.13 review. Bank/pharmacy/library/mall also support routes.

lessons.title: Ways to Travel
lessons.goal: Identify transport and connect it to familiar journeys; explicitly practise a bus, a train and an airplane.
lessons.known: Bus, car and bike: Unit 2. Go to school: current 4.6. Places: 6.1. I/we/they and colors already taught. Do not rely on the superseded go-to-work draft.
lessons.story: Begin with a familiar school journey by bus. Compare train and taxi for the town visit, then walking for a nearby library. A clearly introduced second travel situation extends the same pattern to an airplane and a boat; it is not a magical bus–plane–boat trip.
lessons.bridge: 6.3 names the places where these journeys begin and end; 6.4 shows the physical actions of entering and leaving vehicles.
lessons.evidence: A bus, a train and an airplane all appear explicitly. Bus/car/bike stay ordinary text; train/taxi/airplane/boat/walk/by are this lesson’s yellow targets. No unintroduced going, ride, goes, airport or get on yet.
lessons.reuse: 6.4 travel points; 6.5 boarding transfer cases; 6.13 review. Airplane and boat require successful practice in both the transfer cases and review.

lessons.title: Where Are You Going?
lessons.goal: Ask about a current destination and answer with I am, you are, he/she is and we/they are going.
lessons.story: Ana is leaving for the mall. Luis asks her destination. They then talk about a man going to the bank and a woman going to the library. Finally, Ana’s family joins her: we are going to the mall, while an outside observer describes the same group as they. Every question is followed by the answer it requests.
lessons.known: Unit 3.3: am/is/are + action; Unit 3: personal pronouns. Unit 6.1: destinations. Unit 6.2: by bus/train/taxi and walking. This new lesson prepares the destination before the boarding story.

lessons.goal: Use the destination question with six new venues and travel points.
lessons.known: 6.1 places; 6.2 vehicles; 6.3 Where are you going? and going to; known next to and family members.
lessons.story: Visitors start at their hotel. The family’s outing is the museum, with a post office and movie theater located nearby. Find the bus stop for that outing. A clearly announced later journey connects the hotel, taxi and airport; airplane is retrieved as the reason for this travel point.
lessons.bridge: Learners can now name the destination, vehicle and departure place. 6.4 connects those nouns to boarding and leaving.
lessons.evidence: Keep post office, movie theater and museum visually distinctive. The airport trip is a separate episode. No borrowing untaught get on/off to assess this lesson.
lessons.reuse: 6.6 neighborhood landmarks; 6.8 route destinations; 6.13 review. Airport and movie theater need explicit later successful-path targets.

lessons.title: A Trip to the Mall
lessons.goal: Describe a short trip with a destination, boarding, travel, getting off, walking, an errand and a return.
lessons.known: 6.3: I am going to…; 6.4: bus stop and hotel. Unit 4: first, then, after that, finally. Unit 5: wants and complete polite requests. Vehicles and places already known.
lessons.story: Ana is going to the mall for juice. First she walks to the bus stop, gets on the bus and travels to the mall. Then she gets off and walks to the entrance. She uses her familiar café request. After that, a taxi takes her to the hotel; she gets out and the outing ends. A marked transfer example applies on/off to the train after this story is complete.
lessons.bridge: Once learners can complete a transport action, they need to describe exactly where to board and get off. 6.5 introduces those spatial relationships.
learn: I get out of the taxi.
lessons.evidence: This is the earlier 6.4 example, now 6.5 after inserting Going. Use get ON/OFF a bus/train/airplane/boat and get IN/OUT OF a car/taxi. First/then/after that/finally are known, not yellow. Express the destination with I am going to the mall before the action; the unverified purpose-infinitive to go to is not silently introduced. Train/car and later airplane/boat transfers need connected entry–journey–exit examples, not additions inside Ana’s bus–taxi outing.
lessons.reuse: 6.11 ticketed journey; 6.13 review; 6.14 mission. Car/taxi in/out also recur in the review return trip.

lessons.title: Finding Places in the Neighborhood
lessons.goal: Locate destinations using near, far from, between and across from, then make a useful travel choice.
lessons.known: Where is…?, next to, and; all earlier Unit 6 venues; going and walking.
lessons.story: Ana wants to find the library from the hotel. Luis first establishes which places are near and far, then pinpoints the library between two landmarks and across from the mall. Ana has enough information to walk to the correct building. Use one stable neighborhood with explicit wide and close views.
lessons.bridge: These relative locations prepare left / right from a clearly fixed viewpoint in 6.6.
learn: The library is near the hotel.
La biblioteca está cerca del hotel.
The airport is far from the hotel.

The library is between the bank and the pharmacy.
La biblioteca está entre el banco y la farmacia.
The library is across from the mall.
La biblioteca está enfrente del centro comercial.
lessons.evidence: Near and next to can both be true. Avoid that false contrast. Spatial scenes must preserve the same geography; do not move buildings to make later answers convenient.
lessons.reuse: 6.8 route clues; 6.10 helper’s answer; 6.13 review; 6.14 mission. Between and far from need explicit cards, not background props.

lessons.title: Which Side of the Street?
lessons.goal: Find a named destination on the left or right from a clear viewpoint.
lessons.known: Places and spatial relationships; Where is…?; going; known personal perspective.
lessons.story: Ana and Luis face the same direction from the hotel entrance. The mall is on their left and the pharmacy on their right. Ana is going to the mall; she confirms the side and finds the entrance. After arrival, a clearly marked second viewpoint introduces the station and the bank without silently reversing left and right.

lessons.evidence: Fix the observer’s orientation before testing either side. Prefer photographed spatial context; a pointing person facing the learner can invert the intended left/right.

lessons.title: Following Directions
lessons.goal: Follow a short, ordered route to a destination, with an instruction and visible consequence at each step.
lessons.known: Known locations, going and sequence markers. This is the first explicit route-command lesson; help-request frames wait until 6.10.
lessons.story: Luis gives Ana a route from the hotel to the museum: go straight, go past the bank, turn left at the corner, cross at the reviewed crossing and stop at the museum. Ana follows it. lessons.evidence: English commands are intentional here. Route geometry, photographed turns and arrival must agree. Then and after that are both valid sequence markers; do not use them as uniquely wrong alternatives.

lessons.title: Finding a Safe Way
lessons.goal: Understand can/cannot in a visible situation, then choose and follow an available route.
lessons.known: Unit 5 fixed Can I have…? is familiar; this lesson explicitly extends can/cannot to route possibility and permission. Earlier directions and places are known.
lessons.story: Ana’s first crossing is unavailable. A clearly pictured signal or barrier establishes why she cannot cross here. Luis indicates an available crossing there. Ana follows the short known route, crosses only where permitted, and continues to the museum.
lessons.bridge: The learner can now understand a helper's positive or negative answer in 6.9.
lessons.evidence: Here/there need an established speaker location. Can/cannot requires observable ability, permission or availability evidence. No traffic-safety inference from a generic street photo.
lessons.reuse: 6.10 helpful alternative; 6.13 review; 6.14 mission. Both polarity forms and here/there must be correct targets.

Recognize.scene: A clearly identified open, permitted crossing is visible farther along.
Recognize.task: Distinguish locations with explicit pointing and safe crossing evidence.

Recognize.es: No pueden ir en tren.
Recognize.scene: Reviewed closure cue and unavailable train access are explicit.

lessons.goal: Ask for departure and arrival times, then use them in one achievable journey.
lessons.known: Unit 4 whole-hour questions, days and parts of day; all Unit 6 transport functions. Does…leave/arrive is explicitly introduced as a bounded new question frame.

lessons.title: Mission: Meet at the Museum
lessons.goal: Use directions, transport, help and times to reach a family meeting at the museum.
lessons.known: All prior teaching; no new English. Spanish establishes the goal and each unfamiliar supported mechanic.
lessons.story: Ana must reach the museum to meet her family. She identifies their destination, locates the bus stop, asks a helper for a usable route, chooses the correct service, checks its times, gets a ticket, boards, gets off, follows the final walking directions and reaches the family. One continuous trip, not a second review or a series of disconnected side quests.
lessons.bridge: Finish with arrival and a brief successful exchange, ready to use these functions in later A1 situations.
lessons.evidence: These ten rows are chapters, not ten runtime cards. Expand only into purposeful supported sub-beats. Existing mission acceptance requires at least 32 listening decisions and four speaking gates; the final flow and coverage must be demonstrated before authoring is called complete. No five-stage learner shell, new mechanics or mini-game filler.
lessons.reuse: No new language; resolves one goal and proves communicative transfer.

Mission.en: Where are they going? / They are going to the museum. / I am going to the museum.
Mission.es: ¿Adónde van? / Van al museo. / Voy al museo.
Mission.scene: Family’s destination and Ana’s goal are established before the first challenge.
Mission.task: Understand the meeting place; a voice gate states Ana’s destination.

Mission.en: The bus stop is near the hotel. It is across from the bank.
Mission.es: La parada está cerca del hotel. Está enfrente del banco.
Mission.scene: Stable mission neighborhood and starting viewpoint.
Mission.task: Use listening and spatial clues to find the actual stop.

Mission.en: Excuse me. Can you help me? / Sorry, no.
Mission.task: Understand the heard refusal and approach a different helper.

Mission.en: Can you help me? / Yes. / How do I get to the bus stop? / Go straight. Turn right.
Mission.es: ¿Puede ayudarme? / Sí. / ¿Cómo llego a la parada? / Siga derecho. Gire a la derecha.
Mission.scene: Second helper provides a coherent route to the stop.
Mission.task: A speaking gate asks for help; supported listening decisions follow the route. Long spoken question is not a tile target.

Mission.en: You cannot cross here. You can cross there.
Mission.es: No puedes cruzar aquí. Puedes cruzar allá.
Mission.scene: A clearly blocked crossing and a visible permitted alternative on the same route.
Mission.task: Resolve the obstacle and continue toward the stop.

Mission.en: Which bus goes to the museum? / The blue bus goes to the museum.
Mission.es: ¿Qué autobús va al museo? / El autobús azul va al museo.
Mission.scene: Ana reaches the transit point and identifies the service.
Mission.task: Successful listening choice determines the bus, not a decorative route label.

Mission.en: What time does the bus leave? / The bus leaves at nine. / What time does the bus arrive? / The bus arrives at ten.
Mission.es: ¿A qué hora sale el autobús? / Sale a las nueve. / ¿A qué hora llega? / Llega a las diez.
Mission.task: Ask in a speaking gate; hear departure and arrival before selecting the itinerary.

Mission.en: Can I have a ticket, please? / The ticket is two dollars. / Here is your ticket. / Thank you.
Mission.es: ¿Me da un boleto, por favor? / El boleto cuesta dos dólares. / Aquí está su boleto. / Gracias.
Mission.scene: Counter encounter maintains clerk, customer, price and ticket state.
Mission.task: A voice gate requests the ticket; listening decisions cover price and receipt.

Mission.en: I get on the blue bus. The next stop is the museum. Then, I get off the bus.
Mission.es: Subo al autobús azul. La próxima parada es el museo. Luego bajo del autobús.
Mission.scene: Departure, travel, announcement and arrival occur in order.
Mission.task: Board the chosen service and use the announcement to get off at the correct stop.

Mission.en: Go past the library. Turn left. The museum is on the right. Finally, I am at the museum.
Mission.es: Pasa la biblioteca. Gira a la izquierda. El museo está a la derecha. Finalmente estoy en el museo.
Mission.scene: Final short walk ends with the established family at the museum.
Mission.task: Follow each heard clue, identify the correct building, then complete the meeting. Optional final voice gate confirms arrival.
